Q653601.summary: Carved in oak and life-size, the Gero Cross shows Christ dead upon the cross: his head sinks onto his shoulder, his eyes are closed and his body sags heavily from the arms. It is the oldest large sculpture of the crucified Christ north of the Alps and the earliest known Western image of Christ on the cross as dead rather than triumphantly alive. Set today within a Baroque gilded sunburst, it still draws pilgrims in Cologne Cathedral more than a thousand years after it was made.
facts: It was commissioned by Gero, Archbishop of Cologne (d. 976); its early date was confirmed by dendrochronology in 1976.
The figure is 187 cm high with an arm span of 165 cm; the halo and cross-pieces are original, but the Baroque surround was added in 1683.
Thietmar of Merseburg, writing in 1012–1018, records that the cross originally stood above Gero's grave.
Q653601.notes: Worklist date 960 refined to c. 965–970 (Wikipedia). The paint and gilding have been renewed (a repainting of 1904 is recorded).

cur:monumental-naples-baptistery-traditi.summary: Standing on a blue globe against a deep blue ground, the haloed Christ in golden robes holds out an unrolled scroll to Peter, who approaches with covered hands carrying a cross on his shoulder; a palm tree rises behind. The scroll reads DOMINUS LEGEM DAT, 'the Lord gives the law'. The opposite side, with Paul, is almost entirely lost.
facts: The baptistery of San Giovanni in Fonte beside Naples Cathedral is one of the oldest in the West; its building is dated to the 4th century, and its construction is attributed to Bishop Severus (362–408) or to later bishops.

Of the scenes once set within garlands around the dome, four survive: the Traditio Legis, the Samaritan woman with the Wedding at Cana, the Miraculous Draught (or Peter on the water), and the women at the tomb.
